title: A finite-time singularity of Calabi flow on projective space

issues.location: sections/parabolic.tex Lemma ana:short and Lemma ana:schauder (proof of the distributional-regularity part)
issues.description: Fixed-scale existence for the outer zero-data Cauchy problem, and the regularity of distributional solutions, are taken from external sources (Huang2026 Thm 2.4, Hormander1961 Thm 5.1, DongZhang2015). The uniform estimates are proved in the paper, but existence depends on these citations, which I could not check here. This is not a gap; the cited results are standard in kind.
issues.evidence: "Fixed-scale existence and uniqueness follow from \cite[Theorem~2.4]{Huang2026}, with the trivial real line bundle, r=4 ..."

coverage:
I read every section: introduction, geometry, profile, parabolic, flat, compact, and the certificate appendix. Checks I made independently:
(1) Geometric reduction. Checked by hand: the scalar curvature formula S = n(n+1) - K(H); the center identity S(p) = 110(1 - H(t,0)); the flow sign chain dt(1/v) = AH = d_t u'' and Phi_t = -K = S - Sbar; the sphere Laplacian L on invariant functions, derived from the metric; the eigenvalue factorization A = (-L+n+3)(-L+2n+4); the Euler identity with P(D) = (D-2)(D-1)(D+9)(D+10); the self-similar profile reduction; and the positivity multiplier x + (1-x)G.
(2) Profile. Used sympy to check the ODE coefficients (B = 751/4, C = -1215/4) and the change-of-variables constant. Also checked that L(-3j) takes the stated values and that the residual of the four-term tail polynomial cancels exactly through t^4. Checked the origin recurrence and its Banach-algebra constants. Computed numerically the D_0 roots, the projection matrix Gamma, M_0..M_2, the nonreal response bound, the Lipschitz constant (.567 < .57) and the homogeneous constant (.352 < .36). Checked the Brouwer matching argument.
(3) Certificate. Reran certificate.py, arithmetic_allowances.py and tail-check.py from a scratch copy with assertions on; all passed. Then traced the analytic interpretation: the complex-disk Gronwall bound H2 < .1236, the Cauchy tail, the product perturbation, the endpoint error recursion (.1056R), the bootstrap (12.17R < 14R) and the final projection bounds.
(4) Flat inverse. Checked the similarity change of variables, the linearization coefficients A = G^2 and B_f = -yG'/G, the parametrix and Volterra construction, the compactness of P - P_c, and the spectral split with delta = 2gamma in (0,1). Checked the source decay identity and the annulus L^2-to-X upgrade, which uses delta > 0.
(5) Gluing. Checked the expansion of the nonlinearity N(V); the mismatch coefficient scalings O(b^2); E_c = O(b^-4), which gives a Y-size of b^(2-2delta); the cutoff nesting (chi_i, chi_b, chi_o, kappa) and the exact cancellation in P D_app = I + (R_i + J_o); the smallness of J_o by interpolation; the uniformity of C_D and C_N; the order of choosing eps, then beta, then eta; positivity; and V(t,0) = O(rho^(-1+delta)). Also checked the product corollary, including the KE normalization.
I did not independently verify the cited external Schauder and existence theorems.
main_claim: There is a smooth U(10)-invariant Kähler metric in the Fubini–Study class on CP^10 whose Calabi flow exists smoothly only on a finite interval [0, T*). At the origin p, the scalar curvature blows up like a(T* - t)^(-1/2) with a = -110 G'(0) > 0. This disproves Chen's conjecture that the smooth Calabi flow exists for all time, even in a class that contains a cscK metric. The same singularity carries over to products CP^10 x Y.
sibling_notes: The board for family 352 was empty when I checked, so no sibling reports were available and none affected this audit. I posted my verdict there.
